newsitem.title: USA: Clinton hails resumption of Mideast talks.
newsitem.headline: Clinton hails resumption of Mideast talks.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Sunday hailed the planned resumption of talks between Israeli and Palestinian negotiators in the self-ruled Gaza Strip and said the United States would do everything possible to help.

"The president calls on the parties to conduct these discussions in a spirit of partnership and goodwill in order that tangible results be achieved as soon as possible," the White House said in a statement.

"Israelis and Palestinians deserve to fulfill their aspirations for peace, security and prosperity," the White House said in the statement, which was released in the western New York town where Clinton was preparing for Sunday's debate with Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole.
The debate was the first of two that the men were scheduled to have before the Nov. 5 U.S. presidential election.

"These talks are expected to continue until major outstanding issues are resolved," the White House said. "The United States will do everything possible to assist the parties to achieve early progress."

"(Secretary of State Warren) Christopher's meetings today with the Israeli and Palestinian leadership demonstrate the commitment of the United States to foster rapid, tangible progress toward lasting peace," it said.
Clinton sent Christopher to the region for the first day of talks in the Gaza Strip. The talks were scheduled to resume later on Sunday.

Christopher met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jerusalem on Sunday to urge him to make swift progress on peace moves with the Palestinians. He was also due to hold a separate meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
Clinton announced the talks on Wednesday at the end of a two-day summit in Washington with Arafat, Netanyahu and Jordan's King Hussein.

The emergency summit, which ended with no tangible achievements other than the decision to resume talks on Sunday, was called by Clinton following clashes between Israelis and Palestinians in which more than 70 people died.
The clashes were triggered by Israel's having opened a new entrance to an archaelogical tunnel near the al-Aqsa mosque in Jerusalem, Islam's third-holiest site.
